prompts.display_text: Pin Martin's Cove, where the Martin handcart company sheltered in 1856.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on Martin's Cove in Wyoming, where the Martin handcart company sheltered while waiting for rescue in 1856.
prompts.citation: Martin's Cove: Mormon Trail Site page; Church History Topics, Handcart Companies, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: In 1856 winter storms trapped the Willie and Martin handcart companies and two wagon companies on the plains of present-day Wyoming. The Martin company sheltered in this cove while awaiting rescue. About 250 of the nearly 1,500 stranded people died, and over 300 rescuers came from Utah.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a dedicated temple whose capital has no temple at any stage.
prompts.text_original: A country with at least one dedicated temple but no temple at any stage named for its capital city (as of November 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Five temple countries have no temple, built or planned, in their capital. Australia (Canberra), Canada (Ottawa), Germany (Berlin) and the Netherlands (Amsterdam) all built in bigger cities instead. Côte d'Ivoire's temple is in Abidjan, not the official capital Yamoussoukro. Bolivia is left out because its capital status is split between Sucre and La Paz.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: 5 dedicated, none in the capital Canberra.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: 9 dedicated, none in the capital Ottawa.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: 2 dedicated, none in the capital Berlin.

answers.name: Côte d'Ivoire
answers.fact: 1 dedicated, none in the capital Yamoussoukro.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: 1 dedicated, none in the capital Amsterdam.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where President Russell M. Nelson met with Saints on a 2018 or 2019 ministry tour, temple dedications excluded.
prompts.text_original: A country where Church President Russell M. Nelson spoke to or met with members on a ministry tour in 2018 or 2019 (not a temple dedication).
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.note: Puerto Rico (Sept 2, 2018) omitted as a territory.
prompts.summary: In his first two years as Church President, Russell M. Nelson circled the globe several times. He spoke in Spanish in Santo Domingo, met Peru's president in Lima, addressed stake broadcasts in Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay, and visited Bangkok, Bengaluru, Singapore, Apia and Bogota.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: October 20, 2018: Peru's president Martin Vizcarra met President Nelson at the presidential palace; Nelson spoke in Spanish to thousands of Saints in Lima.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: August 25, 2019: President Nelson presided at a devotional in Bogota with more than 10,000 Colombian Saints.

answers.name: Dominican Republic
answers.fact: September 1, 2018: President Nelson met with Saints in Santo Domingo and delivered his entire address in Spanish.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: October 21, 2018: President Nelson visited El Alto on his South American trip and spoke at a devotional broadcast to all stakes.

answers.name: India
answers.fact: April 19, 2018: President Nelson and Elder Jeffrey R. Holland spoke to Saints at a devotional in Bengaluru.

answers.name: Paraguay
answers.fact: October 22, 2018: President Nelson's talk to members in Asuncion was broadcast to all stakes in Paraguay.

answers.name: Singapore
answers.fact: November 20, 2019: President Nelson visited Singapore as part of his Southeast Asia ministry and spoke in Bukit Timah.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: April 20, 2018: President Nelson and his wife Wendy visited Bangkok and spoke to members.

answers.name: Uruguay
answers.fact: October 25, 2018: President Nelson spoke to members in Uruguay from a large center in Montevideo, broadcast throughout the country.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: May 18, 2019: President and Sister Nelson spoke with Samoa's prime minister at a devotional for Saints in Apia.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a city that still goes by the same name it has in the Bible.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country with a city that is still a city under the same name it carries in the Bible
prompts.citation: Acts 18:24; Numbers 21:30; Job 6:19; Esther 1:2; Wikipedia, Tayma and Madaba
prompts.note: Site is in the West Bank or Gaza; a player may reasonably pin ISR as well.
prompts.summary: Many Bible cities never stopped being cities. Jerusalem, Damascus, Athens, Rome and Alexandria are all living places under their scripture names. Lesser known survivors include Madaba in Jordan, the Medeba of Numbers 21:30, Shush in Iran, the Shushan of Esther, and Tayma in Saudi Arabia, the Tema of Job 6:19.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jerusalem, Nazareth and Beersheba are all living cities today under their Bible names.

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Athens and Corinth, where Paul preached, are still Greek cities (Acts 17-18).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Rome, where Acts ends, is still Italy's capital (Acts 28:16).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Jericho, Bethlehem and Hebron are West Bank cities still called by their Bible names.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Damascus, where Saul was baptized, is still Syria's capital (Acts 9).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Alexandria, home city of Apollos, is still Egypt's second city (Acts 18:24).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Tyre and Sidon remain Lebanese coastal cities (Matthew 15:21).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Tarsus, Paul's birthplace, is a city in southern Turkey today (Acts 21:39).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Paphos, where Paul met Sergius Paulus, is still a Cypriot town (Acts 13:6).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Shush is the Shushan of Esther 1:2 and Nehemiah 1:1.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Madaba is the Medeba of Numbers 21:30 and still carries the name.

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Tayma in northwest Arabia is the Tema of Job 6:19 and Isaiah 21:14.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a current member of the First Presidency or Twelve served his full-time mission as a young man (October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A country where a member of the First Presidency or Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, as of October 2026, served his full-time mission as a young man.
prompts.citation: Official leader biographies, churchofjesuschrist.org/learn and Church News, read 4 Nov 2026 (Holland died 27 Dec 2025; Causse and Gilbert called 2025-26)
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, ten of the fifteen men in the First Presidency and Quorum of the Twelve served full-time missions as young men, in nine countries from the United Kingdom and Germany to Argentina, Japan, Sweden, Taiwan and Brazil. The official biographies of Dallin H. Oaks, Henry B. Eyring, Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Patrick Kearon and Gerald Causse list no young full-time mission. Jeffrey R. Holland, who served in Britain, died December 27, 2025.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Quentin L. Cook served as a full-time missionary in the British Mission.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Ronald A. Rasband served in the Eastern States Mission, 1970-72.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: D. Todd Christofferson served in Argentina.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Ulisses Soares served in the Brazil Rio de Janeiro Mission.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: David A. Bednar served in southern Germany.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Neil L. Andersen served in the Paris France Mission, 1970-72.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Gary E. Stevenson served in the Japan Fukuoka Mission; Clark G. Gilbert served in the Japan Kobe Mission.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Dale G. Renlund served in Sweden.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: Gerrit W. Gong served in the Taiwan Mission, 1973-75.
